executiveSummary: Iteration 000042 introduces the `nvst auto` pipeline command and fixes `audit prototype` state persistence. All three user stories (US-001, US-002, US-003) are fully implemented. The `auto` command is correctly registered in `src/cli.ts`, `src/commands/auto.ts` follows the one-file-per-command convention, and `runAuditPrototype` now writes `prototype_audit.status = 'completed'` and `updated_by` to state after a successful run. All 7 functional requirements comply, all 35 unit tests pass, and typecheck returns clean.

verificationByFR.notes: `auto` command registered in `src/cli.ts` with `--agent <provider>`, `--force`, and `--yolo` options. Confirmed by test US-001-AC01 and direct CLI inspection.
`runAuto` implemented in `src/commands/auto.ts`, following the one-file-per-command convention.
`runAuto` reads state and calls `assertGuardrail` with condition `requirementStatus !== 'approved'` and an explicit error message.
`runAuto` calls `runCreatePrototype`, `runAuditPrototype`, `runRefactorPrototype` in sequence, forwarding `provider`, `force`, and `yolo` to each.
No try/catch in `runAuto`; sub-phase errors propagate unmodified, halting the chain.
After a successful agent invocation `runAuditPrototype` sets `prototype_audit.status = 'completed'` and calls `writeStateFn`. The `writeState` is only called when `result.exitCode === 0`.
`state.updated_by` is explicitly set to `'nvst:audit-prototype'`. `state.last_updated` is automatically stamped by `writeState` (line 53 in `src/state.ts`), confirmed by test US-003-AC02.

verificationByUS.notes: All 9 acceptance criteria verified by tests in `it_000042_us-001-auto-pipeline.test.ts`. `interactive: false` is correctly forwarded to audit, and create/refactor retain default interactive behaviour.
All 5 acceptance criteria verified by tests in `it_000042_us-002-auto-requirement-guard.test.ts`. Strict/relaxed guardrail modes, `--force` bypass, and warning output all behave as specified.

All 5 acceptance criteria verified by tests in `it_000042_us-003-audit-state-update.test.ts`. State write, `updated_by`, `refactorAllowed` guard, and the absence of state writes on failure are all covered.

minorObservations: No integration / end-to-end test exercises the full `nvst auto --agent <provider>` path from the CLI entrypoint through all three phases. Unit tests mock sub-commands, so an actual subprocess regression is not caught automatically.

The `--agent` option is required for `nvst auto` but Commander does not mark it as `.requiredOption`; missing `--agent` is caught by `validateAgent` which prints an error and returns `null`, preventing the command from running — acceptable but not the idiomatic Commander pattern.

The guardrail in `runAuto` does not print a warning in `strict` mode (only throws), whereas `--force` in strict mode prints a warning and proceeds. This is consistent with the existing guardrail contract but differs slightly from the 'warning is still printed' language in AC04 — test US-002-AC04 confirms `force + strict` prints a warning, so this is compliant.
conclusionsAndRecommendations: The implementation is fully compliant with all functional requirements and user stories. The code is clean, typechecks pass, and test coverage directly maps every acceptance criterion. The only notable gap is the absence of an integration test for the full CLI flow. Recommended next step is to proceed to `refactor prototype` to address the minor observations above (particularly adding an integration smoke-test and considering `.requiredOption` for `--agent` in the `auto` command).
